title: USS Kearny torpedoed
body:
A German torpedo tore into an American warship seven weeks before Pearl Harbor. Eleven sailors never came home.

17 October 1941. Off Iceland, a German wolf pack was savaging a British convoy, and the destroyer USS Kearny raced in with three other U.S. destroyers to help the overwhelmed Canadian escorts. Through the night Kearny dropped depth charges. Then U-568 put a torpedo into her starboard side.

Eleven men were killed and 22 wounded. Her crew sealed off the flooding in the forward fire room and kept her moving on the aft engine. She limped into Iceland at 10 knots two days later.

The United States was not yet at war, but it no longer felt like peace. Ten days later President Roosevelt told the nation, "America has been attacked." Two weeks after Kearny was hit, the USS Reuben James was sunk.
photoNote: Kearny at Reykjavik on 19 Oct 1941, two days after the hit. The torpedo hole is visible midships. U.S. Navy photo 80-G-28788, public domain.
threads:
Seven weeks before Pearl Harbor, a German torpedo hit an American warship.

17 October 1941. USS Kearny was helping defend a British convoy off Iceland when U-568 struck her starboard side. Eleven sailors were killed and 22 wounded.

Her crew sealed the flooding and nursed her into Iceland two days later. Roosevelt soon told the nation, "America has been attacked."
